chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If a man from you is afflicted with a wound (khuraj) or a boil (dummal), let him bandage it and let him treat it with oil or butter.

key_terms.الْخُرَاجُ: A wound or sore, specifically one that discharges pus or fluid.
key_terms.بِزَيْتٍ: With oil (typically olive oil), a permitted treatment substance.
key_terms.سَمْنٍ: Butter or ghee, another permitted treatment substance.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for treating wounds or boils while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that applying oil or butter (samn) to wounds or boils does not invalidate the Ihram state, addressing the scholarly debate on whether topical applications constitute 'using perfume' or 'covering the head' which require compensation. It establishes a practical medical exception for pilgrims, ensuring that necessary treatment does not incur the penalty of fidya (ransom) typically associated with breaking Ihram restrictions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If a man from you is injured with injury, or the pimple, so let him bandage it, and let him effect treatment with oil or butter’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If something appears on your skin like a pimple or so, you can bandage it and use ghee or oil as medicine.’”
